classes.name: VuGlassesHidManager
classes.role: Host HID opener for Vu/View glasses: waits for UsbDevice attach, requests permission, starts Glasses HID service (IGlassesHid / GlassesManager), then openUsb. Companion glasses USB path is USB HID, not AOA.

classes.name: UsbStarryManager
classes.role: StarryNet USB accessory manager: registers USB_ACCESSORY_* broadcasts and opens android.hardware.usb.UsbAccessory via UsbAccessoryManager.connect (AOA PFD), not glasses HID.

classes.name: UsbStarryNetDiscoverer
classes.role: Discovers AOA accessories only if manufacturer==ICCOA and model==CarLink; parses AOA preamble as car IDs. Not a glasses protocol.

classes.name: UsbAccessoryManager
classes.role: UsbManager.getAccessoryList / openAccessory wrapper used by UsbStarryManager.

classes.name: UsbNative
classes.role: ucar AOA bulk IN/OUT via libusbio; car-link path, not MYVU glasses HID.

classes.name: UsbPermissionHelper
classes.role: UsbManager.requestPermission for View-glass UsbDevice VID/PID used by the HID path.

why_not: If a glass enumerated, the companion would speak USB HID (VuGlassesHidManager + IGlassesHid) to VID 10821 (0x2A45) / PID 8272 (0x2050) View/Vu devices. Star Air (XGA010C) user firmware has no gadget/HID/AOA stack, USB-C does not enumerate (PROTOCOL.md / INVESTIGATION.md: charge path, BLE-only), and VuGlassesHelper.f() would reject any other VID/PID. StarryNet USB is ICCOA CarLink AOA, not glasses. Enabling USB R/W without enumerating that HID gadget cannot satisfy the host.
other_skus: HID USB is for Vu/View display glasses (package vu, ViewGlasses*, StarV View / XGG010C), not Star Air / XGA010C. StarryNet USB accessory is ICCOA CarLink cars. Star Air host protocol in this repo is BLE.
conclusion: Enabling USB R/W on Star Air is NOT the companion HID/AOA path unless firmware enumerates a USB gadget the host can open. The intl companion speaks USB HID to View glasses (VID 0x2A45 / PID 0x2050) via VuGlassesHidManager; AOA is CarLink-only. This XGA010C user image has no gadget stack and never enumerates, so host HID/AOA cannot start. BLE remains the Star Air channel.
